Title: CE Changes/Cards I *Expected* But Didn't Happen

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
Okay, I've been meaning to make a post like this since GenCon but just never
got around to. Some slightly similar posts have popped up, but this post is
specifically to discuss changes and cards that people wish or *expected* White
Wolf to have made in the Camarilla Edition, but which were not done. Here's
some of mine:

(No particular order)

#1. Tone done Parity Shift a bit.

#2. Slightly change Anarch Revolt to give it a bit more of a cost (being
discussed in another thread).

#3. Limit Freak Drive to once a turn (really expected them to do this,
especially with it becoming an Uncommon).

#4. Make Disarm less nasty.

#5. (Not exactly a change) but I did expect at least some of the ante cards to
be reprinted (or a new ante card). Even though most people don't play ante,
many card games continue to print cards using the ante feature.

#6. Was expecting some sort of global Dementation infection as opposed to all
of the new reprinted vampires (a la Tajdid). Not sure whether what they did was
better or worse but I did expect something that would using old Dominate Malks
to be a bit easier.

#7. Expected a Praxis Seizure: New York card.

#8. Ban Arika! =P

That's just off the top of my head. Anyone have any other thoughts?

Halcyan 2

I'm kinda surprised they didn't just go ahead and tweak all the
Protean Strike: Combat Ends cards along with everything else. Gangrel
will have a slight advantage over the others until Anarchs comes out
(when I expect that will be finally addressed).

I would have liked to see more symmetry in the Rarities of cards.
Right now, there are lots of Clan (and other) rares that are
designated R2, many of which are either not generally strong or less
useful because they're unique. For example:

Current R2 = Malkavian Prank, Storm Sewers, Tremere Convocation,
Fragment of Nod, J.S. Simmons, Mr. Winthrop, Tasha Morgan, Rumors of
Gehenna and Ghoul Retainer (last two aren't unique, but I'd have made
'em R1 anyway for usefulness)

All of these could have easily been made R1s and no one would have
complained. Now, Discipline rares are much better in quantities, since
multiples can be included in a deck and they'll still be useful in
decks. Most disciplines work across several clans and can have upwards
of 170 (Dominate in 1+2 and 2+3) vampires for certain disciplines, so
people really need and want those cards. Tthe number of crypts that
can make use of these rares is much higher. For example:

Current R1 = Murder of Crows, Cat Burglary, Abandoning the Flesh,
Dominate Kine, Day Operation, Psycic Veil, Fists of Death,
Entrancement, and Infernal Familiar

I really wish the above rarities would have been switched. Even though
some of those R1s aren't particularly useful, many of them really are
and would find their ways into more decks. IMO, Clan specific cards
should be slightly more powerful and focused than normal Rares since
there are only 20 or so vampires available for a given clan. This
would mean they could be nice R1 "chase" cards (though I'm not
advocating WW really go there).

member (11 pool + 3 or more turns to bring him or her into play, that is, an

action, and as a political action it is, you have to make it pass, which is an
addional drawback.

have to include some Direct Intervention, or Delaying Tactics, rushes
(targetting IC members), Derange, Fear of Mekhet, etc., etc., etc.

PTO is not a card you should have in great numbers in your deck, because it is
only effective against non-Camarilla vampires. And if there are non-Camarilla
vampires at a table, I would only play PTO on a those controlled by my predator
or prey (depending on the situation).

easily defeated.

Oh, yes, I know PTO hurts, but Archon Investigation, Fear of Mekhet, Meddling
of Semsith, Lapse, and many other cards hurt too, and that is not enough reason
to say they are overpowered ;-)

squabbling amongst themselves and not finding a way to get rid of the Revolts with

Delaying Tactics wind up being fairly useless, as you say. I think the cost of
the Delaying Tactics will make some difference against ARs, but I agree that it
will be marginal. Still, I don't see the problem with Anarch Revolts in the
first place.

As someone who's watched lots of tournament games he hasn't been playing
in, I'm never certain of this.

Lots of situations turn into "He's not the threat, *he's* the threat".
Walking round and watching people's hands and the like, it often seems
that a number of players (not all, but certainly a large number, even if
still a minority) *would* actually be better off just going for their
prey - their enemy being taking their eye off the ball, with a highly
competent diplomatic contingent on the table doing that for them.
Remember: you only need two VPs for a table win, 3 for a guaranteed
table win. A lot of games like this can continually turn into "He's the
threat! Kill him! *dies* Now *she's* the threat! Kill her!" This is
something demonstrably Garfield wanted to avoid with the predator/prey
dynamic.

However, assuming we allow for "taking out the strongest player" as a
useful tactic - which it very definitely is, on an unspecified number of
tables - are we 99% certain that a Non-Camarilla vampire will turn up on
the strongest player? I'd say not.

Playing ICs (predominantly) is a very, very difficult design decision if
you *aren't* planning to get them out quickly (if your deck is primarily
about bringing one/more out, as opposed to having one or two there for
when you see your predator isn't about to swarm you to death). If your
IC decks aren't designing decks for high probabilities of good Zillah's,
Tomb or Info Highway flow, then they might as well be dead in the water.

deck and you include the combative cards for getting into combat (be
that permanents with Freak Drive, Bum's Rush, or whatever), you include
the cards that make the deck *work*. Speeding up IC decks makes them
work. Sure, it can be a bit of a bind. But if you don't include them,
that's three turns to bring out Alexandra (or whoever you're choosing) -
four (!) if you get first transfers. Just like if you don't include
Bum's Rush (or one of multiple variants) in your rush deck, you'll find
getting into combat a tad more tricky. And yes, playing those
Bewitching Orations in a bruise-and-vote deck is a bit of a bind, but
hey, it could be worse.

You pick what's best for your deck. And almost every deck has some
element of "uninteresting" staple cards which they need to play. That
doesn't make them expensive, it tends to make them very necessary.

tactics with regards getting vampires out. It simply has to, or it'll
just die when its predator is the weenie swarm from hell. This isn't
unique to PTO, it isn't unique to IC decks even. Any big vampire deck,
or single vampire deck, is going to be doing similar things. (Such
will, of course, vary slightly in their composition, as suits each
deck.)

Inner Circle members comes out in two turns (or, if dunlucky, three, but
pretty much certainly not the four turn horror). True of any IC deck
that wants to be fast and effective. So, let's try a few situations to
go with this.

Situation: Inner Circle deck plays, say, Obfuscate bleeds with large
vampires, Presence, Dominate whatever. The "uninteresting" set-up for
it, was, say, 2 Information Highways, 5 Zillah's Valley. (Just picking
numbers randomly.)

Situation: Inner Circle deck does some neat trick with Alexandra,
Chimerstry and Illusions of the Kindred. (Ben Peal's idea, as I
recall.) Similar set-up, to get out an Alexandra fast and replace her
if she dies (or you Golconda them, say).

Situation: The Inner Circle deck gets out vampires fast, and uses Govern
the Unaligned to generate pool and get out other vampires fast too.
Similar set-up.

Situation: PTO. It uses a similar set-up to the above. Does it get a
much bigger swing than others? I'm still unsure. But it's just the
same set-up as other IC decks bringing out vampires fast. Sure, bring
out vampires slowly if you want. And don't put Bum's Rush variants in
your rush deck. That's not a lot of resources, that's playing the right
cards in the right deck.

I'm unsure whether I like, say, Arika being able to come out fast,
Secure Haven herself (optional), Mind Rape a vampire, Clan Impersonate
them and then burn them. Or even just throwing in half a dozen PTOs
into a deck, throwing them at the vampires that get in their way, at
either pred or prey most of the time.

special (prevent one damage each combat) and her FOR (no need to fear
Kiss of Ra, which is VERY important). This version of deck (as played
on Slovak National Qualifier) use only two version of Omaya but you

4 bleed your prey with your army of midcaps and weenies

Crows combo. With only 20% percent of combat cards (and three combat
permanents) you can still torporize lots of minions.

Board mainly.
